A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NAMI research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched across the revision.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark scores, human evaluations, inference timings, ablations, and generated-image examples.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds training-resource measurements, bridge-strategy comparisons, and image-editing examples.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 revises the specified training interpolation to use normalized within-window time and global-time conditioning. Appendix D adds an editing procedure that shares first-stage outputs and switches subsequent prompts. The architecture and linear BridgeFlow remain unchanged; these revisions do not establish that existing models were retrained.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds an evaluated image-editing scenario, illustrated by dog-attribute edits in Figure 27; v2 discussed editing only prospectively. The training-data sources and GenEval, DPG-Benchmark, and NAMI-1K coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: New Table 7 compares BridgeFlow against Pyramid Flow's upsampling with renoising, upsampling with an MLP, and Pixel Shuffle with a CNN. These alternatives were not evaluated in v2. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark and human-evaluation tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds a training-efficiency evaluation at resolution 256, batch size 768, and eight 80-GB A100 GPUs, measuring throughput, GPU hours, and peak memory. It also specifies a 256-resolution bridge comparison. Existing benchmark protocols and ablation sample counts are retained.

E4.justification: The analyses expand substantially beyond v2's flow/model decomposition, layer allocation, and time-window ablations. v3 directly tests the central BridgeFlow design against alternative transitions, quantifies training-resource efficiency, and adds an editing case study. The inference-component timing analysis is retained from v2's Appendix C, not newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests for these experiments. The five-annotator evaluation procedure is unchanged, and the new tables also report point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 and the original plotted results are unchanged. New Table 6 reports NAMI versus FLUX-based throughput of 274 versus 241 images/s and memory of 55 versus 67.6G. Table 7 adds bridge timing and quality results, and Figure 27 adds editing outcomes; these are additional findings, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: v3 revises interpolation direction and stage-time normalization in Sections 3.1–3.2 and Algorithm 1. New Appendix C introduces Gaussian conditional-path assumptions and an affine distribution-alignment argument in Equations 5–8. It does not provide a formal proof of the asserted velocity consistency.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same four contributions: multi-resolution training, approximately 64% faster inference, BridgeFlow, and NAMI-1K. The conclusion now references an editing demonstration, supporting applicability already proposed in v2 rather than redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 and Appendix C add explanations contrasting learnable linear bridges with nonparametric renoising and nonlinear mappings, including claims about trajectory curvature and optimization stability. v3 interprets Table 7 as a speed-quality tradeoff; the MLP and CNN alternatives nevertheless achieve better individual quality metrics.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 and new Appendix E disclose that the internal data comprise approximately 100,000 fine-tuning pairs, with CogVLM2 recaptioning, multistage filtering, and human assessment. v3 also supplies hardware/batch details for the efficiency comparison and three-layer specifications for bridge alternatives. The internal-data description is added disclosure, not evidence of a newly introduced dataset.

R1.justification: v3 more explicitly positions BridgeFlow against Pyramid Flow's renoising. It replaces the LAPGAN citation to Lai et al.'s super-resolution work with Denton et al.'s generative-model paper, adds residual-network and sub-pixel-convolution references, and removes several background citations. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Section 3.3 and the conclusion receive localized rewrites, appendix sections are added and reorganized, and the former appendix timing discussion moves into Section 4.4. Author/header text and reference wording also change, while most existing narrative remains closely matched.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 6–7 and the editing Figure 27, relocates v2's timing Figure 26 to main-text Figure 9, and moves table captions above their tables. Existing figure imagery is retained, with limited reflow and a new supplementary-material heading.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, the new training-resource measurements and bridge alternatives directly strengthen empirical support for the efficiency claims, while Appendix E improves data transparency. The gain is limited: main benchmark results remain unchanged, and the revised interpolation still conflicts with the unchanged velocity-target signs in Equations 2 and 4. The new Gaussian discussion also does not prove its stronger stability assertions.
